analogy: Assign each new meeting to the room that becomes free first.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
hints: Sort bookings by arrival time and keep end times of currently occupied rooms.
A room can be reused only if its previous customer has left strictly before this customer arrives.
If no room is free, allocate a new one; remember each original customer's assigned room.
algorithm: Sort bookings by arrival. Reuse a room whose end time is strictly less than the new arrival; otherwise create one. Store the chosen room ID by original booking index and print the maximum ID plus assignments.
correctness: If the earliest-ending room has end>=arrival, every occupied room is still in use, so a new room is necessary. If its end<arrival, reusing it is valid and does not increase the room count.
example: Bookings [1,4) and [4,5) still need different rooms under the problem's strict rule, since the first customer leaves at the exact arrival time of the next.
